rows.evidence: Q1: Case study section (Figures 2-4, Table 3) - the authors compute their own dekadal anomaly percentiles and drought onset/duration/severity statistics for the 2014 Senegal drought from CHIRPS, H SAF, ESA CCI, SWI, NDVI and VODCA datasets.
rows.notes: The paper is labelled a review; only the Senegal case study is own analysis, and it is borderline primary. That case study shows microwave SM and VOD anomalies tracking the spatio-temporal development of a drought; it does not report crop development or crop-yield monitoring results of its own. Yield-related statements (Carrao 2016, Padhee 2017, Modanesi 2020, Vroege 2021) are cited from other work and do not count. The own result (drought/soil-moisture deficit detection) is at best a precondition for the claimed yield monitoring.

rows.evidence: Q1: Case study section (Figures 2-4, Table 3) - own calculation of anomaly percentiles and drought statistics over Senegal from satellite rainfall, soil moisture and vegetation datasets.
rows.notes: The study contains no result on irrigation scheduling or water conservation. Irrigation is only mentioned incidentally (irrigated area along the Mauritanian border appeared less drought-affected; satellite SM implicitly includes irrigation water, citing Massari et al.). The own result is coarse-scale (0.1 degree, dekadal) drought monitoring, which is at most a precondition for irrigation scheduling optimization, not evidence of it.

notes: Document is a review article with an embedded Senegal case study; Q1 answered yes on the strength of the case study's own data analysis, but the case study addresses drought monitoring only, not crop yield or irrigation scheduling. Full text appears complete.
